title: A walk whose app died says the app died
goal: When a scripted run of the app ends because the app itself quit, the sweep reports it as 'no done.json' and moves on. That is the same words it uses for a run that simply never finished, so a crash reads as a slow walk. The app has been aborting on every layer rename since last night, it left twenty-one crash reports on disk, and four sweeps in a row called it seven walks that took a hundred and eighty-seven seconds each. Have a run that ended in a crash say so, and say what the crash was.
notes:
REPRODUCED here at 2026-09-18 01:26 local on HEAD 33132430:

  $ Scripts/playtest-all.sh --no-build unique-layer-names
  unique-layer-names-walk    186s  FAILED  no done.json
  ==> 0 passed, 1 failed

and at the same moment a fresh report appeared at ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Photonz Probe-2026-09-18-012738.ips, EXC_CRASH SIGABRT, top app frame EditorState.renameLayer. Nothing in the sweep output mentions it.

Where the wording is made: Scripts/playtest-all.sh:149-151

    reason="$(printf '%s' "$out" | sed -n 's/.*\"error\" : \"\(.*\)\",*$/\1/p' | head -1)"
    verdict="FAILED  ${reason:-no done.json}"

The fallback is used whenever the walk left no error behind, which covers both 'the app died' and 'the walk never finished', and those are not the same news. A crash also costs the full per-walk timeout, which is why seven crashing walks burn 22 minutes of every sweep.

What a fix has to hand: the probe's own exit is visible to Scripts/playtest.sh, and macOS writes an .ips into ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports within a second or two of the abort, named for the app and stamped with the time, so a run that ends badly can look for one newer than its own start. Whichever route is chosen, the point is the WORDS the sweep prints, because those words are all the loop reads.

Why this is filed against the loop rather than left alone: this is the loop's only whole-app regression signal, and it did not merely miss the crash, it actively described it as something else. Twenty-one crashes over six hours and four sweeps went by with nobody looking, and the p0 that came out of it (renaming-a-layer-stops-crashing-the-app) was found by a manager pass reading a stack trace, not by the thing whose job it is.
acceptance: A walk whose app quit unexpectedly is reported as a crash, not as 'no done.json', and the line names the top app frame from the crash report
The sweep summary counts crashes separately from ordinary failures, so a sweep that crashed once is never read as a walk that is merely slow
A walk that genuinely runs out of time still reports as running out of time, and is distinguishable from a crash
Verified against the real thing: the reproduction below currently prints 'no done.json' and afterwards prints a crash line naming EditorState.renameLayer
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
